req.title: POST-only actions reject GET
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 405 when GET is used on /<id>/delete.

doc.reasoning: The requirement specifies that the system should return an HTTP 405 status code when a GET request is made to a POST-only endpoint. This ensures that the endpoint is protected against incorrect HTTP method usage. The tests will cover positive, negative, and boundary cases to ensure robustness against common mutations.

tests.name: test_post_only_action_rejects_get
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test' user
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})

# Attempt to GET a POST-only endpoint
r = client.get('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 405

tests.name: test_post_only_action_with_post_method
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test' user
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})

# Correctly use POST method on the endpoint
r = client.post('/1/delete')
assert r.status_code == 302
assert r.headers['Location'] == '/'

tests.name: test_post_only_action_boundary_case
tests.executable:
from flaskr import create_app
import tempfile, os
fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(); os.close(fd)
app = create_app({'TESTING': True, 'DATABASE': path})
client = app.test_client()

# Log in as 'test' user
client.post('/auth/login', data={'username': 'test', 'password': 'test'})

# Boundary case: Attempt to GET a non-existent post id
r = client.get('/0/delete')
assert r.status_code == 405
